top_choice_rationale: Katori and Ye's optical lattice clock is a distinct invention (magic-wavelength cancellation of the lattice light shift with many atoms interrogated in parallel) beyond the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. It is reproduced in Sr, Yb and Hg at 10^-18, already used for tests of constants, dark matter and geodesy, and the two-name allocation needs no forced exclusion. P002 is a close second: a secure, broad discovery, but its three names leave Cao, other experimental groups and earlier twisted-bilayer theorists outside the citation. P003 is mature but has a contested third seat (BHZ, Hasan) and overlap with the 2016 prize. An award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my documented connections (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur) do not overlap with optical clocks, moire materials or topological insulators, though I note an experimentalist bias toward instrument-driven results.
